Compare other items in the lot, positions on the same jig, processing records and storage conditions. Compare affected and unaffected items under consistent conditions rather than looking only at defective ones.

paragraphs.title: Control product disposition while investigating
paragraphs.text:
Even before identifying a cause, keep suspect items separate from acceptable goods. Identify and hold them, determine the potentially affected scope, and follow designated authority for shipment decisions. A worker cannot approve shipment merely because a defect looks small.
After corrective action, verify improvement using the same inspection method. A mark becoming invisible under different lighting or changing the recorded position does not prove improvement. Also check how reprocessing affects dimensions and performance.

paragraphs.title: Workplace reasoning
paragraphs.text: A component looked normal immediately after drying but developed local discolouration by the next day. Provide the responsible person with the affected position, storage location, packaging and drying/rinsing records. Do not prematurely conclude storage caused it; also compare unaffected items held under the same conditions.

terms.meaning: A defect where the film separates from the substrate and bulges.
A change in colour.
A defect where plating is absent from an area that requires it.
A proposed explanation to be checked by investigation.

mfg1-surface-lesson-017.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 10 on appearance and possible causes, and 6 organizing example information. Make an affected/unaffected comparison table in 7 minutes and review shipment authority in 3.
safety: Do not touch defects with bare hands or independently wipe them with chemicals.
Follow authorized decisions for reprocessing and shipment.
mfg1-surface-lesson-017.summary:
Distinguish a defect’s appearance from its cause.
Compare lots, positions and histories.
Identify and hold suspect items even while the cause remains unknown.

mfg1-surface-lesson-018.title: Understand pretreatment and bath control in hot-dip coating
mfg1-surface-lesson-018.objective:
Distinguish hot-dip coating from electroplating.
Explain the purposes of drying and process control.

paragraphs.title: Form a coating in a molten-metal bath
paragraphs.text:
Hot-dip coating immerses a substrate in molten metal and forms a film through withdrawal, cooling and related stages. It differs from electroplating, which uses current to deposit metal from solution. Hot-dip galvanizing is a representative example.
Conditions vary with bath metal, substrate combination, shape and dimensions. Even for corrosion-resistant applications, thicker is not automatically better. Check required dimensions, appearance, alloy layers and other specified properties.

paragraphs.title: Degreasing, pickling, fluxing and drying
paragraphs.text:
Removing oil and oxides is important for proper contact with molten metal. Flux treatment helps preserve the surface after pickling and assists reaction between substrate and molten metal. Use the specified liquid and sequence for the product.
Drying before immersion is important to reduce molten-metal splashing. Do not assume an item is dry when it is wet or retains liquid internally. Follow the prescribed checks and equipment requirements for its shape.

paragraphs.title: Do not control the process by temperature alone
paragraphs.text:
Temperature, immersion time, withdrawal, cooling and finishing influence the film. A normal equipment display does not authorize processing when material or pretreatment is unverified. Retain history and investigate preceding stages if an unplated area or another defect appears.
High-temperature baths, splashes and handling create serious hazards. A lesson on principles is not equipment-operation authorization. Learn exclusion zones, transport methods and emergency actions through training, and work only within your instructions.

paragraphs.title: Workplace reasoning
paragraphs.text: Two same-shaped items differ: one looks dry and the other retains liquid in a recess. Do not judge them equivalent from visible flat areas alone. Follow drying and shape-specific checks. If uncertain, hold the item and explain the reason to the responsible person rather than immersing it.

terms.meaning: A coating method using a molten-metal bath.
Placing an item into a liquid or similar medium.
Acid treatment to remove surface oxides and similar material.
Material that prepares the surface and assists reaction with molten metal.

mfg1-surface-lesson-018.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 10 on stages and 6 on the drying example. Create a pretreatment/main-process control table in 7 minutes, then contrast electroplating in 3.
safety: Do not put wet or unverified items into molten metal.
Keep away from high-temperature baths and follow exclusion zones and transport procedures.
mfg1-surface-lesson-018.summary:
Immersion in molten metal forms the coating.
Pretreatment and drying are essential controls.
Confirm conditions for material, shape and required quality.

mfg1-surface-lesson-019.title: Separate the mechanisms of electroless and dry coating
mfg1-surface-lesson-019.objective:
Explain differences between external current, reduction reactions and gas-phase processing.
Do not infer safety or uniformity from a process name alone.

paragraphs.title: Chemical plating without external current to the item
paragraphs.text:
Electroless plating forms metal films chemically rather than passing current from an external supply to the item as in ordinary electroplating. Methods include reducing-agent processes and displacement processes that react with the substrate. Do not treat their reactions as identical.
Some reduction processes require pretreatment such as applying a catalyst. In an autocatalytic process, the deposited film catalyses further reaction. Applying the method to a nonconductive substrate requires appropriate pretreatment and material compatibility.

paragraphs.title: No external current does not mean no control
paragraphs.text:
Electroless processes still require concentration, temperature, pH and agitation control. A process that can produce relatively uniform films on complex shapes does not automatically solve inaccessible areas or unsuitable pretreatment.
Nickel-phosphorus, copper and gold processes are selected for applications and required properties. Do not decide a material change from a teaching example alone; check process instructions and quality requirements.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish PVD and CVD by formation mechanism
paragraphs.text:
Dry PVD deposits material physically, using evaporation or sputtering. CVD forms a film through chemical reactions involving gaseous precursors. Both differ from ordinary wet plating by immersion in an aqueous bath.
“Dry” does not mean no hazardous substances or exhaust. Vacuum, high temperature, power, precursor gases and exhaust treatment require controls appropriate to the machine and method. Follow dedicated training and procedures for operation and maintenance.

paragraphs.title: Workplace reasoning
paragraphs.text: A worker is about to apply electroless-bath conditions to an item specified for PVD. Because film-formation mechanisms differ, those settings cannot be transferred. Confirm process type, substrate, required pretreatment and equipment with the responsible person before proceeding.

terms.meaning: Plating by chemical reaction rather than externally supplied current.
A substance that supplies electrons to reduce another substance.
A substance that promotes a reaction.
A general term for methods forming films using a gas phase or similar environment.

mfg1-surface-lesson-019.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 10 on the three mechanisms and 6 on the process-sheet example. Compare external current, reactions and equipment in 7 minutes, then review names versus safety in 3.
safety: Check equipment-specific high-temperature, vacuum, gas and electrical hazards even in dry processes.
Do not independently modify or open chemical or gas equipment.
mfg1-surface-lesson-019.summary:
Electroless plating uses chemical reactions.
PVD uses physical deposition; CVD uses chemical reaction.
Different methods have different controls and hazards.

mfg1-surface-lesson-020.title: Check wastewater segregation and treatment status
mfg1-surface-lesson-020.objective:
Do not judge wastewater safety by clarity or pH alone.
Confirm wastewater routes and abnormality reporting.

paragraphs.title: Rinse water still contains components
paragraphs.text:
Rinse water from plating or anodizing may contain chemicals and metals carried over from preceding stages. Clarity does not prove absence of harmful substances. Prevent unmanaged discharge to rivers or seepage into the ground.
Treatment requirements are not limited to pH. Control conditions depend on substances, concentrations and discharge destinations. The responsible environmental staff verify current permits and rules; this lesson does not set legal limits or authorize discharge.

paragraphs.title: Do not mix different streams
paragraphs.text:
Segregate wastewater and spent liquids into designated streams according to composition and treatment method. If labels or piping identification are unclear, hold the transfer and check rather than judging by colour. Classifying liquids as acidic or alkaline does not make every mixture permissible.
Some mixtures generate hazardous gas or heat. Learners must not mix small quantities to test them or dilute waste down a drain. Trained personnel follow prescribed methods for sampling, transfer and treatment.

paragraphs.title: Check treatment results separately from leakage
paragraphs.text:
Even after separating solids, a clear liquid may retain dissolved components. Judge treatment through required analysis and checks rather than appearance. Removed solids also require prescribed waste management.
A leak around floors or pipes can still affect the environment after drying. Report from a safe position to prevent escalation, recording location, time, suspected stream and visible conditions. Do not independently neutralize an unknown leak.

paragraphs.title: Workplace reasoning
paragraphs.text: Liquid at a treatment outlet has become clear, but analytical results are pending. Do not assume it is ready for discharge; keep it awaiting the prescribed confirmation. If another leak is found, do not add a different waste liquid without knowing its pH; report to the responsible person.

terms.meaning: Water discharged from a process or similar source.
Separating according to type and treatment method.
Components present in dissolved form in a liquid.
Escape of liquid or another substance from containment.

mfg1-surface-lesson-020.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 10 on wastewater routing and 6 on the example. Explain clarity, pH and analysis as different checks in 7 minutes, then summarize leak-report information in 3.
safety: Do not mix, neutralize or dilute unknown waste liquids.
Do not approach a leak; follow workplace evacuation and reporting procedures.
mfg1-surface-lesson-020.summary:
Clarity and pH alone do not guarantee safety.
Composition-based segregation and treatment confirmation are necessary.
Report and investigate leaks even after drying.

mfg1-surface-lesson-021.title: Record exhaust, noise and environmental controls
mfg1-surface-lesson-021.objective:
Consider exhaust and noise impacts together.
Use records to verify environmental improvements.

paragraphs.title: One control can create another impact
paragraphs.text:
Surface treatment requires controls for chemical mist, solvent vapour and dust according to the source and equipment. Exhaust and scrubbing equipment reduce worker and environmental exposure, but fans and similar machinery may create noise.
Stopping exhaust to reduce noise can increase a different hazard. Rather than lowering one number alone, consider equipment function, work conditions and surrounding impacts together. Operational changes require responsible staff evaluation and authorization.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish ambient conditions from discharge control
paragraphs.text:
Distinguish evaluating the surrounding environment from controlling substances and quantities leaving equipment. Check site conditions according to equipment scope, location and time. Specific legal limits and notifications must be managed from current sources.
Little odour does not prove safety. Do not judge gas concentration by smell; use prescribed inspection and measurement. Record discovery time and equipment status for unusual sound, exhaust changes, leaks or complaints too.

paragraphs.title: Plan, act, check and revise improvements
paragraphs.text:
Environmental management identifies which activities cause which impacts and defines targets, actions and verification. Continual improvement is important in ISO 14001’s approach. Certification does not automatically make every emission or task compliant.
The 3Rs—reduce use, reuse and recycle—must preserve quality and safety. Do not mix chemicals or change waste classifications without authorization to save liquid. Record before-and-after results under comparable conditions to verify effects.

paragraphs.title: Workplace reasoning
paragraphs.text: After a complaint about night-time fan noise, the responsible staff organize operating times, work activities, noise and exhaust-equipment conditions. Workers report rather than stop the fan themselves. After corrective action, verify required exhaust performance as well as noise under comparable conditions.

terms.meaning: Removing gas from equipment or work areas, with treatment where required.
Unwanted sound that affects living or working conditions.
The burden an activity places on the environment.

terms.reading: けいぞくてきかいぜん
terms.meaning: Repeated verification and review to improve performance.

mfg1-surface-lesson-021.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 10 on combined impacts and 6 on the night-time example. Create a before-and-after record in 7 minutes, then review how the 3Rs and safety coexist in 3.
safety: Do not stop exhaust or safety equipment without authorization to reduce noise or electricity use.
Do not approach and sniff an unknown odour or gas to identify it.
mfg1-surface-lesson-021.summary:
Manage both exhaust and noise.
Distinguish environmental conditions from equipment discharges.
Verify improvements with records under comparable conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-022.title: Connect daily and periodic inspections
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-022.objective: Distinguish daily checks from planned inspections, and treat unchecked items as unconfirmed.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Preventive maintenance is an approach to checking equipment condition to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing it after a breakdown. Daily checks cover specified items before work and at other designated times to detect small changes early. Periodic inspections follow a plan and examine details that daily checks alone may not reveal. Performing one does not permit omission of the other.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: This morning’s checklist includes leaks, unusual sounds, and cover condition. A completed periodic inspection yesterday does not remove the need to check for leaks this morning. If insufficient lighting prevents a check, record why it remains unconfirmed instead of marking it normal, and consult the responsible person about how to check and whether operation is permitted. A completion mark must reflect work actually performed.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: Link equipment number, date and time, condition, and action in the inspection record. Comparable observations are more useful for tracking change than simply writing “same as usual.” Repair and internal inspection require authority and safety measures. Dismantling beyond the scope you can inspect is not evidence of greater diligence.

terms.meaning: Activities to check and maintain equipment condition to prevent failures and accidents.
Checking specified items before daily use or at other designated times.
Detailed inspection at planned intervals.
A condition that has not yet been verified.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-022.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: For imaginary equipment, write three daily-check items and two periodic-inspection items, then create an example record for an item you cannot check.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: For internal inspection and repair, follow equipment-specific procedures and authority requirements for stopping, energy isolation, and prevention of restart.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-022.summary: Daily and periodic inspections complement each other. Do not replace “unconfirmed” with “normal”; record observed facts.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-023.title: Separate density from a material’s response to force
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-023.objective: Distinguish density, elasticity, plasticity, and toughness, and avoid selecting material from one property alone.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Density is mass per unit volume. Objects of the same volume can have different masses when their materials differ. Elasticity means deformation recovers after force is removed; plasticity means deformation remains. Hardness and toughness—the ability to resist fracture under impact and similar loading—are also different properties. “Light” or “hard” alone does not establish suitability for an application.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Consider a component of volume 20 cm³. Assuming densities of 2.70 g/cm³ for aluminum and 7.87 g/cm³ for iron, their calculated masses are 54.0 g and 157.4 g respectively. However, lower mass does not authorize replacement of a specified iron component with aluminum. Required strength, deformation behavior, temperature conditions, and other factors must also be checked. Density varies with the material and alloy.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: A bent sheet can spring back partly when force is removed. Separating elastic recovery from the plastic deformation that remains helps explain the final shape. Do not determine material grade solely by appearance, color, or how heavy it feels; check the material identification and records. Material substitution involves design and quality decisions.

terms.meaning: Mass per unit volume.
The property of recovering deformation when force is removed.
The property of retaining deformation after force is removed.
Resistance to fracture under impact and similar loading.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-023.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Calculate masses for volume 10 cm³ using the same assumed densities, and list three selection conditions other than density. Also give separate examples of elasticity and plasticity.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Do not machine or ship unidentified material as the specified grade based only on appearance.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-023.summary: Density relates to mass; elasticity and plasticity relate to recovery of deformation. Check hardness, toughness, and application conditions separately.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-024.title: Distinguish steel heat treatments by purpose
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-024.objective: Distinguish the purposes of quenching, tempering, annealing, and surface hardening.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Heat treatment changes metal structure and properties through heating and cooling conditions. In typical steel treatments, quenching is used to increase hardness, while tempering adjusts hardness, toughness, and other properties after quenching. Annealing may soften the material to improve machinability. Not every metal hardens in the same way under identical heating and cooling.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: An imaginary tool-component process sheet specifies “temper under the specified conditions after quenching.” Do not assume the component is complete simply because quenching made it hard; confirm completion of the entire sequence, including tempering and inspection. Similarly, an instruction to soften material before further machining cannot be replaced with quenching because the names sound similar.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: Surface hardening improves surface properties, so the interior and surface are not necessarily in the same condition. Welding also creates a heat-affected zone around the melted area. Match the material, treatment purpose, temperature, time, cooling conditions, and inspection results. This lesson explains the concepts; it is not an operating instruction for setting heat-treatment conditions.

terms.meaning: A treatment that increases hardness in steel and certain other materials through appropriate heating followed by rapid cooling.
Reheating after quenching to adjust hardness, toughness, and related properties.
Heating and cooling for purposes such as softening or structural adjustment.
The surrounding region whose structure or properties changed because of heat from welding or another process.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-024.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: For increasing hardness, adjusting properties after quenching, improving machinability, and hardening only the surface, write the corresponding treatment name and the process records to check.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Furnaces, hot material, and cooling media present hazards. Do not change temperatures or cooling methods at your own discretion.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-024.summary: Connect treatment names to their purposes. Do not confuse quenching and annealing; confirm the whole specified process.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-025.title: Distinguish the motions of lathes, milling machines, and drill presses
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-025.objective: Explain cutting-machine applications from the motions of the workpiece and tool.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Cutting removes material with a tool to form the required shape. A lathe mainly rotates the workpiece against a tool to machine features such as outside diameters. A milling machine rotates the tool and uses relative movement between tool and workpiece to produce flats and grooves. A drill press rotates a drill to make holes. Distinguishing what rotates helps explain machine roles and danger areas.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Consider a sequence that finishes a round bar’s outside diameter, then makes a flat mounting face and a hole. A lathe, milling machine, and drill press are possible choices, but the actual route is determined by the drawing, machine capability, and approved process sheet. Do not assume a round starting material must stay on a lathe throughout. A machining center has automatic tool-changing capability and can perform several operations.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: Cutting produces heat and chips. Cutting fluids and coolants help remove heat, reduce tool wear, and carry away chips, but adding fluid alone does not prove an unusual sound or poor finish has been resolved. Compare clamping, tooling, and cutting conditions with the records. The source figure numbers have corrections, so identify references by page and machine name.

terms.meaning: The material or component being machined.
A machine tool that rotates the workpiece and removes material with a cutting tool.
A machine tool that uses a rotating cutter for features such as flats and grooves.
A machine tool equipped with automatic tool-changing capability.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-025.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: For outside-diameter machining, flat machining, and drilling, make a table of what rotates, the intended shape, and the required setup checks.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Do not touch rotating parts. Follow the equipment’s stopping and safety-confirmation procedure before chip removal or measurement.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-025.summary: Distinguish cutting machines by tool and workpiece motion. Separate possible equipment choices from the actually approved process.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-026.title: Distinguish grinding and polishing objectives
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-026.objective: Separate dimensional accuracy from surface finish and do not judge completion by appearance alone.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Even if a shaft looks shiny, an outside diameter above the upper limit is not dimensionally acceptable. Conversely, an acceptable size does not establish that the required roughness has been met. Refinishing also removes material and changes size, so confirm the available machining allowance and approved disposition before proceeding.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: The wheel or polishing medium must suit the material, processing purpose, and equipment conditions. Do not substitute a similar-looking item without permission. Link the processed location with its inspection result and do not use gloss as a substitute for measurement. This lesson does not replace the education or qualifications required for wheel replacement or trial running.

terms.meaning: Material removal in small amounts using abrasive grains in a wheel or similar tool.
A process that conditions a surface using abrasives and similar media.
An abrasive tool that holds abrasive grains.
Material left to be removed during finishing or other machining.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-026.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Create an inspection note separating requirements and checking methods for outside diameter, surface roughness, and gloss, and list two checks before rework.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Follow required training and procedures for wheel replacement and trial running. Keep hands away from rotating wheels and polishing areas.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-026.summary: Distinguish grinding and polishing purposes. Do not treat dimensions, roughness, and gloss as one acceptance item.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-027.title: Compare how welding, casting, and plastic forming create shapes
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-027.objective: Distinguish joining, molten-metal solidification, and plastic deformation of solids.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Welding joins members using heat, pressure, or related means. Casting pours molten metal into a mold and solidifies it into shape. Plastic forming applies force to solid material and retains deformation to form a shape. These mechanisms differ from cutting, which removes material. Examples of plastic forming include press work, forging, and rolling.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Compare three objectives: joining two sheets, making a body with complex spaces in a mold, and pressing a sheet into a bend. Welding, casting, and press work are possible choices respectively. However, do not select a method from shape alone; check material, required strength, production quantity, and later processes. Several methods can be combined, such as machining after casting.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: A good-looking joint, a casting removed from its mold, or a pressed item that appears to have the correct shape does not alone prove that all requirements are met. Confirm process-appropriate internal, dimensional, and visual inspections. Consider heat-induced changes around a weld and springback after forming, and consult before changing methods outside your authority.

terms.meaning: A technique for joining members using heat, pressure, or related means.
Forming a shape by pouring molten metal into a mold and solidifying it.
Forming solids by applying force and using deformation that remains.
Plastic forming by pressure or blows applied to metal.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-027.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Compare welding, casting, and press work in a three-column table covering material state, shape-forming mechanism, and main checks.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Follow specified equipment, protection, and training for process-specific hazards such as welding light and fumes, hot molten metal, and press entrapment.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-027.summary: Distinguish joining, solidification, and plastic deformation. A product is not necessarily made by one process alone.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-028.title: Match roughness parameters and measurement conditions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-028.objective: Distinguish Ra from Rz and check dimensional acceptance separately from roughness acceptance.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: An imaginary instruction requires “Ra no greater than 0.8 μm,” but the result field only states “Rz 3.2 μm.” You cannot decide acceptance by comparing the numbers alone. The parameters differ, so confirm a result measured for the specified Ra under the required conditions. A separate acceptable outside-diameter result cannot substitute for roughness acceptance.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: A stylus roughness instrument converts needle motion into a signal to examine irregularities. Location, direction, and surface contamination can affect the result, so follow the specified measurement method. Record parameter name, value, unit, and location, aligning the conditions for comparison. Take care not to damage a precision surface through the stylus or cleaning.

terms.meaning: The degree of small irregularities on a surface.

terms.reading: さんじゅつへいきんあらさ
terms.meaning: The Ra parameter expressing roughness as an average magnitude.

terms.reading: さいだいたかさあらさ
terms.meaning: The Rz parameter based on peak and valley height in a roughness profile.
A fine needle that contacts a surface to detect irregularities.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-028.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Create a roughness record with fields for parameter, value, unit, location, and conditions. Write a confirmation request when only Rz is available for an Ra requirement.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Do not measure a moving workpiece. Protect the stylus and precision surface according to the specified handling method.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-028.summary: Do not directly compare values from different roughness parameters. Judge dimensions and roughness against their own requirements and measurement conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-029.title: Read voltage, current, and resistance in a DC resistor circuit
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-029.objective: Explain Ohm’s-law conditions and the difference between voltmeter and ammeter connections.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Voltage is measured in V, current in A, and resistance in Ω. Under applicable conditions, the voltage across a resistor and its current obey V = I × R. With the same voltage across a fixed resistor, a larger resistance gives a smaller current. This does not mean that an entire machine may always be calculated as a single resistor.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: In a paper-based DC resistor circuit, assume 24 V across 12 Ω. The current is I = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 A. At the same 24 V, a resistance of 24 Ω gives 1 A. The example concerns a simple circuit with fixed resistance. Do not use this result directly as a motor’s starting current or an AC device’s current.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: On a circuit diagram, a voltmeter connects in parallel across the part being measured; an ammeter connects in series so the branch current passes through it. This is study of what the connections mean. Connecting an ammeter directly across a power source can cause a dangerous short circuit. Actual measurement requires the operator’s applicable qualifications and training, suitable instrument ratings, procedures, and work authorization.

terms.meaning: The electrical difference between two points, measured in V.
The flow of electric charge, measured in A.
A quantity indicating opposition to current flow, measured in Ω.
A connection between the same two points.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-029.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: On paper, calculate current for 18 V and 9 Ω, then compare with 18 Ω. Draw voltmeter and ammeter positions on a paper circuit diagram; do not connect real equipment.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Perform this activity only on paper. Do not connect an ammeter directly across a power source or measure energized circuits without authorization.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-029.summary: Check the simple DC-resistor conditions before calculating. A voltmeter is parallel and an ammeter series; the connections mean different things.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-030.title: Distinguish plastic molding by product shape
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-030.objective: Explain differences among injection, blow, compression, extrusion, and reinforced-plastic molding.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Injection molding shapes flowing resin in a mold. Blow molding uses air to produce hollow forms, while extrusion continuously pushes material through a die to make long products of constant cross-section. Compression molding shapes material by pressure within a mold. Reinforced plastic combines resin with reinforcement such as fibers. Materials and solidification mechanisms differ between methods.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Consider a complex small case, a hollow container, and a long tube with a repeating cross-section. Injection, blow molding, and extrusion are possible choices, but a hollow shape does not necessarily mean blow molding. A tube is also hollow, yet has a continuous constant cross-section. Decide from material, quantity, molding conditions, and the approved process as well as shape.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: Some materials solidify through cooling, while others cure through a chemical reaction. An open mold alone does not establish a safe touching temperature or completion of curing. The specified process includes removal, cooling, and inspection. Record resin name, material lot, equipment, and conditions; do not mix materials or change conditions without permission.

terms.meaning: A method forming a shape by introducing flowing resin into a mold.
A method producing hollow products by inflation with air.
A method continuously pushing material through a die to form a constant cross-section.
Resin or a similar material becoming solid through a reaction.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-030.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: For a case, container, long hose, and fiber-reinforced bathtub, make a table of possible methods and conditions still to confirm.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Observe procedures for removal and cleaning, addressing mold entrapment, hot resin, and reaction-generated heat.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-030.summary: Consider material together with hollow or constant-cross-section features. An open molding machine does not prove cooling or curing is complete.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-031.title: Match coating purposes with application methods
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-031.objective: Distinguish corrosion protection, appearance, and added functions; compare spray, electrostatic, and electrodeposition coating.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Coating does more than add color: it protects the substrate, improves appearance, and can provide functions such as insulation or heat shielding. Brush coating spreads paint with a tool; spray coating atomizes it onto the surface. Electrostatic coating uses forces from electric charge, while electrodeposition forms a film electrically in a bath. Similar names do not mean identical processes.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: An outdoor component has uniform color on the visible front but missed coating on the rear. If corrosion protection is a purpose, an attractive front alone does not justify acceptance. Compare the specified surfaces, film condition, required thickness, and inspections with the instruction. Do not simply add another layer on your own; confirm the reprocessing method with the responsible person.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: A functional paint does not provide its performance at every thickness or under all conditions. Align the paint, substrate, application, and drying or curing conditions. Both finish inspection and chemical handling are necessary; color alone does not identify the contents. Check equipment grounding, ventilation, and other requirements under the procedure for that coating method.

terms.meaning: Applying paint to a surface to provide protection, appearance, or other functions.
Using electrostatic forces to deposit paint.
Forming a paint film electrically in a bath.
The film formed on a surface by paint.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-031.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Write one requirement to check for corrosion protection, appearance, and insulation, and briefly explain differences among spray, electrostatic, and electrodeposition methods.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Follow paint labels, safety data sheets, and specified ventilation, protection, and ignition-control rules. Do not mix solvents or paints without permission.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-031.summary: Do not judge coating by color alone. Match purpose, surfaces, materials, process conditions, and inspections.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-032.title: Choose packaging for protection, identification, and transport
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-032.objective: Explain the roles and limitations of individual wrapping, corrugated boxes, and shrink film.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Packaging protects products from scratches, dirt, moisture, and other hazards, communicates identification, and facilitates transport and storage. Individual wrapping supports separate protection and control; corrugated boxes group items together. Shrink film contracts under heat, but wrapping alone does not guarantee complete impact or moisture protection.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Finished metal parts packed together in a box may contact one another and become scratched during transport. In addition to a strong outer box, check instructions for individual partitions and protection. Before putting different specifications together, verify whether mixed packing is permitted and whether labels and quantities remain identifiable. Do not count similar-looking items together.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: After packing, match the specified product name, specification, quantity, lot, and other information to the contents. A readable label and a correct label are separate checks. Consider package weight, stacking, and handling during opening, and observe storage conditions. Heat-shrink processes also require checking heat effects on the product and packaging material.

terms.meaning: Wrapping products one at a time.
Reducing the effect of impact.
Packaging film that shrinks with heat to conform around products or similar objects.
Making types or conditions distinguishable.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-032.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Design packaging for metal parts that must remain scratch-free, covering individual protection, movement inside the box, identification label, quantity, and storage conditions.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Follow equipment and handling procedures for burns and entrapment at heat-packaging machines and for box or load weight.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-032.summary: Packaging serves protection, information, and transport as well as appearance. Match contents to labels and do not overestimate a material’s protective capability.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-033.title: Compare hot- and cold-rolling conditions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-033.objective: Distinguish how processing temperature affects deformation, dimensions, and surfaces.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Rolling is plastic forming in which material passes between rolls and pressure changes its shape, for example by reducing thickness. Hot rolling heats the material to make deformation easier; cold rolling is introduced here as processing without applied heating. Cold rolling still generates heat during work and does not mean “cold, therefore safe.” Check the process against required thickness, material, and temperature conditions.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Suppose a hot-rolled sheet measures differently while hot and after cooling. Account for thermal dimensional change and check in the specified measurement state. Cold rolling can produce precise dimensions and surfaces, but requires larger forces and can harden the material through working. Neither hot nor cold rolling is superior under every condition.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: In an example plan reducing thickness from 6.0 mm to 4.5 mm, the reduction is 1.5 mm. Relative to the original thickness, it is 1.5 ÷ 6.0 × 100 = 25%. This calculation does not specify an allowable reduction in one pass. Actual pass count and conditions depend on equipment capability, material, and the approved process.

terms.meaning: Plastic forming that passes material between rolls and uses pressure to reduce thickness or otherwise change shape.
Rolling performed with material at high temperature.
Rolling performed without applied heating.
Hardening of material through plastic deformation.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-033.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: Compare hot and cold rolling for force, surface condition, and temperature-related dimensional change. Calculate the thickness reduction and percentage from 8.0 mm to 6.4 mm, keeping the calculation separate from actual process selection.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Observe procedures preventing entrapment between rolls; do not touch rotating parts or material even in cold rolling.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-033.summary: Temperature changes forming behavior and finish. A thickness calculation alone does not determine rolling conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-034.title: Trace the roles of rolling oil and post-treatment
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-034.objective: Distinguish lubrication, cooling, and surface protection from property adjustment after rolling.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Rolling oil controls friction between the rolls and material to help the process run smoothly. It also carries away heat and helps reduce seizure and surface scratching. More oil is not necessarily better; oil type and supply conditions must follow equipment and product instructions. Do not try to address a defect only by changing the amount.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: Suppose linear scratches are found on a rolled sheet. Oil supply is one item to check, but roll and material-surface conditions also need investigation. Record the location, discovery time, affected scope, and oil/equipment records, then report to the responsible person. Do not increase supply without permission and declare the issue resolved simply because later sheets look better.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: After rolling, properties may be adjusted by annealing or the surface may be treated to match the application. Reaching the required thickness is different from completing the required hardness and surface condition. Check the process sheet for post-treatment and inspections, and keep rolled-only items distinguishable from post-treated items.

terms.meaning: Oil used in rolling for lubrication, cooling, surface protection, and related functions.
Appropriately reducing contact friction to facilitate smooth movement.
A defect in which heat, friction, or related effects damage or cause adhesion at contact surfaces.
A process after the main operation that establishes necessary properties or condition.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-034.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: For scratches after rolling, organize observed facts, oil checks, roll checks, and the scope of untreated items. State two post-treatment completion requirements other than thickness.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Check and replenish oil only at specified safe locations and conditions; do not approach rotating rolls.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-034.summary: Rolling oil relates to cooling and protection as well as lubrication. Manage completion of rolling separately from completion of post-treatment.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-035.title: Check aluminum extrusion temperature, dies, and handling surfaces
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-035.objective: Explain constant-cross-section forming and the conditions to investigate for longitudinal lines and cracks.

paragraphs.title: Principle and process role
paragraphs.text: Aluminum extrusion pushes a heated billet through a die to produce a long product with a cross-section corresponding to the die opening. Applications include window frames and heat-dissipating fins. Specified cooling, straightening, and cutting follow extrusion. Product condition depends not only on die shape but also on material, temperature, and speed.

paragraphs.title: A concrete workplace decision
paragraphs.text: A line repeatedly appears at the same location along the product’s length. Die damage or deposits are possible checks, but foreign matter on the runout table receiving the product also needs investigation. Record the line’s position and continuity, and establish with the responsible person where it was introduced. Do not hold a moving product down or clean a hot die on the spot to investigate.

paragraphs.title: Conditions and records to check
paragraphs.text: An excessively low billet temperature raises forming load; excessive temperature can also lead to problems such as surface cracks. Do not assume that simply raising temperature is better. Follow the specified range matching material, shape, and speed. Link the die number, material lot, temperature, speed, and receiving-surface condition in records, and ask the designated person to perform repairs or change conditions.

terms.meaning: A mass of metal used as stock for extrusion or similar processes.
A forming tool through which material passes to obtain its cross-sectional shape.
Correcting bends or similar deviations to the specified shape.
A table that receives and carries the extruded product.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-035.activity:
4 min: Check the terms and the process covered.
10 min: Read the principles and conditions and write differences from similar methods.
7 min: Organize the case decision and its grounds in a diagram or bullet points.
7 min: For a longitudinal line and a surface crack, separately list observed facts to record, equipment/conditions to check, and actions that must not be taken without permission.
2 min: Record key points and matters to confirm at work.
safety: Keep away from hot billets and dies and moving products; perform cleaning, replacement, and repair under stopping and safety-securing procedures.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-035.summary: Control extrusion through cross-section, temperature, and speed together. Do not assume one cause for a line; check both die and handling surfaces.

mfg1-electrical-l022.title: Distinguish coils from capacitors
mfg1-electrical-l022.objective: Explain coil and capacitor structures and functions, checking specifications and residual energy.

paragraphs.title: Similar appearance, different functions
paragraphs.text:
A coil consists of wound wire; some use a magnetic core. Its distinctive feature is the relationship between current and magnetism. A capacitor separates conductors with insulation and stores charge. Size or terminal count alone does not establish whether a part serves as a coil, capacitor, or resistor.
Capacitors include electrolytic, ceramic, and film types with different capacitance, voltage rating, polarity, temperature, and other conditions. Equal capacitance alone does not justify substituting another type. For polarized types such as some electrolytic capacitors, compare documentation with mounting orientation.

paragraphs.title: Separate the initial transient from the settled state
paragraphs.text:
In a basic ideal example, connecting a capacitor through a resistor to a DC source causes charging current, then no current in the fully charged steady state. This is an idealized explanation, not a safety guarantee that ignores real leakage or failure.
Charge may remain after power is switched off. A switch being off does not establish absence of hazardous energy. Do not invent a discharge method or waiting time; follow workplace procedures.

paragraphs.title: Specification comparison example
paragraphs.text: Two capacitors have the same capacitance, but one is rated 16 V and the other 50 V. Equal capacitance does not mean equal specifications. Check polarity, dimensions, temperature, permitted conditions, and operating voltage, and use the approved part number. A resistance reading across a coil also does not mean it functions like a capacitor or resistor.

terms.meaning: A wound-wire component using the relationship between current and magnetism.
A component that separates conductors with insulation and stores charge.
A quantity expressing a capacitor’s ability to store charge.

terms.reading: ていじょうじょうたい
terms.meaning: A condition reached after changes have settled with time.

mfg1-electrical-l022.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, specification comparison 7 min, writing 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Make a table comparing coil and capacitor structure, basic function, and specifications to check. Explain why equal-capacitance 16 V and 50 V parts are not unconditionally interchangeable. Write two Japanese sentences about checks after switching power off.
Self-check: Do you distinguish capacitance from voltage rating and avoid assuming power off means no residual charge?
safety: Do not touch terminals or short them with tools to check capacitor discharge.
Removal and measurement must follow assigned responsibilities and procedures for isolation and confirmation of discharge.
mfg1-electrical-l022.summary: Coils use current and magnetism; capacitors store charge. Do not omit specification matching or residual-energy checks.

mfg1-electrical-l023.title: Transistor amplification and switching
mfg1-electrical-l023.objective: Distinguish the three bipolar-transistor terminals and two functions and check maximum ratings.

paragraphs.title: Match the three terminals
paragraphs.text:
A bipolar transistor has base B, collector C, and emitter E. PNP and NPN types differ in structure and operating polarity. Do not assume all three-lead parts have the same pin order; check each part-number diagram. Similar packages may have different terminal arrangements.
In basic terms, the base input controls collector current. Amplifying small signal changes and switching current on and off have different purposes and operating conditions.

paragraphs.title: Do not select by gain alone
paragraphs.text:
Current gain hFE is the ratio of collector current to base current under specified operating conditions. It is not a universal fixed multiplier; it changes with conditions and the part. Nor can the on state in switching be determined unconditionally from an amplification equation alone.
Parts have maximum terminal voltages, currents, dissipation, and other ratings. A part may control a signal yet overheat or fail beyond those limits. Check the usage conditions and specification restrictions together rather than treating ratings as unrelated numbers.

paragraphs.title: Limit the use of a ratio calculation
paragraphs.text: At one teaching operating point, suppose base current is 0.10 mA and collector current is 8 mA. The ratio there is 8 ÷ 0.10 = 80. This does not establish a constant 80-fold ratio with other loads or unlimited collector current. Explain the result with its conditions, type, and maximum ratings.

terms.meaning: Producing a larger signal from a smaller signal variation.
Turning current on and off.
Specification limits that must not be exceeded.

terms.reading: でんりゅうぞうふくりつ
terms.meaning: The collector-current to base-current ratio under specified conditions.

mfg1-electrical-l023.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, ratio example 7 min, application comparison 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Write the names of B, C, and E and compare amplification with switching. Calculate the ratio for 0.05 mA and 4 mA at one operating point, then state two things it cannot guarantee.
Self-check: Even after obtaining 80, do you avoid claiming a fixed multiplier under all conditions or unlimited output?
safety: Do not replace and energize a part without checking its type and terminal arrangement.
Do not touch a hot or unusually smelling part; follow approved stop and reporting procedures.
mfg1-electrical-l023.summary: Match terminals, purpose, and operating conditions. Gain calculations do not replace maximum-rating checks.

mfg1-electrical-l024.title: Organize ICs and analog and digital circuit functions
mfg1-electrical-l024.objective: Classify IC functions by signal type and distinguish amplification, oscillation, modulation, and demodulation.

paragraphs.title: Consider how signals are handled
paragraphs.text:
Analog signals represent continuously varying quantities, while digital signals use discrete values. Analog functions include op-amp amplification and voltage-regulator supply stabilization; digital functions include logic processing and memory. Similar-looking ICs can have very different functions.
A/D conversion turns an analog quantity into a digital value; D/A does the reverse. These functions bridge signal domains. Explaining input and output with arrows is more useful than memorizing their names as one group.

paragraphs.title: Circuit names and purposes
paragraphs.text:
An amplifier takes a small signal and produces a larger one; an oscillator generates a periodic signal. Making an existing signal larger and generating a periodic signal are not the same operation.
Modulation reflects information onto a carrier, while demodulation extracts information from a received modulated wave. AM varies amplitude, FM frequency, and PM phase. Also distinguish information processing from stabilizing the power supply.

paragraphs.title: Signal-path example
paragraphs.text: For a teaching system sending a continuous temperature-related voltage to a computer, consider: sensor analog signal → necessary signal conditioning → A/D conversion → digital processing. A supply regulator supports the power conditions but does not replace A/D conversion. Check actual signal ranges and supply voltage against the IC specifications.

terms.meaning: A circuit integrating several electronic functions on a small semiconductor structure.
A quantity that can take continuously intermediate values.
A quantity handled as separate, distinct values.
A high-frequency wave used to carry information.

mfg1-electrical-l024.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, signal path 7 min, function organization 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Draw input/output arrows for A/D and D/A. Write one sentence each for amplification, oscillation, modulation, demodulation, and supply stabilization. Tabulate which quantity AM, FM, and PM change.
Self-check: Do you identify A/D as converting a continuous sensor voltage to digital values without confusing it with supply stabilization?
safety: Do not exchange ICs solely because their function names match; check pins, supply, and input ranges.
Use approved low-voltage teaching equipment and procedures; do not inject signals into real equipment without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l024.summary: Understand ICs by input, processing, and output. Amplification, oscillation, modulation/demodulation, and supply stabilization serve different purposes.

mfg1-electrical-l025.title: Computer functions and binary numbers
mfg1-electrical-l025.objective: Explain five computer functions and the CPU, and convert binary using place values.

paragraphs.title: Trace five functions
paragraphs.text:
Input receives external data or commands; memory stores data and programs; control decodes instructions and directs other units; arithmetic performs calculations and logic; output presents results externally. The CPU combines the central control and arithmetic functions.
A factory recording terminal similarly receives a barcode, stores part data, compares it, and displays the result. Do not mistake the screen for the whole computer; separate which function may have a problem.

paragraphs.title: Read binary by place value
paragraphs.text:
Binary uses 0 and 1, with place weights 1, 2, 4, 8… from the right. Decimal 10 is ten, but binary 10 is 1 × 2 + 0 × 1 = 2. The same written digits mean different values in different bases, so identify binary or decimal explicitly.
For example, binary 1101 is 1 × 8 + 1 × 4 + 0 × 2 + 1 × 1 = 13. Add the weights of the occupied places to check. Do not join digits after skipping zeros or read it as decimal 1101.

paragraphs.title: Separate terminal fault observations
paragraphs.text: If a scanned barcode does not update the part number on screen, a read beep alone does not prove input, processing, and display are all normal. Report separately the facts you can check within your role, such as input history, processing results, and display state. Preserve the current condition and job number before deleting data or changing settings.

terms.reading: ちゅうおうしょりそうち
terms.meaning: The CPU, responsible for control and arithmetic.
A unit that retains data and programs.
A number representation using 0 and 1 with place values doubling.
The number on which a positional notation is based.

mfg1-electrical-l025.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, place calculations 7 min, function organization 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Convert binary 1011 and 10010 to decimal, showing place weights. Match terminal operations to input, memory, control, arithmetic, and output. Write a Japanese report separating checked and unchecked facts in the barcode example.
Self-check: Do you obtain 11 and 18 and distinguish CPU from display and successful input from successful processing?
safety: Do not delete production records or change control settings without authorization when handling terminal problems.
Do not send commands to real equipment as a binary-number experiment.
mfg1-electrical-l025.summary: Organize computers by five functions. Identify the base and place values when reading binary.

mfg1-electrical-l026.title: Distinguish printed-board manufacture from component assembly
mfg1-electrical-l026.objective: Distinguish an unpopulated wiring board from an assembled circuit board and explain conductor patterning and mounting.

paragraphs.title: Board structure and component mounting
paragraphs.text:
A printed wiring board has conductor patterns formed on an insulating base. Its process state differs from a board with electronic components mounted and ready to function as a circuit. Avoid using the short name “board” so vaguely that before/after mounting is unclear.
Structures include single-sided, double-sided, and multilayer; forms include rigid, flexible, and combinations. Flexible does not mean any location can be folded any number of times. Check bending locations and conditions in the specifications.

paragraphs.title: Copper to retain and copper to remove
paragraphs.text:
In a process that removes unwanted copper foil, protect the required pattern and remove exposed unwanted copper using an etchant or another specified method. Resist provides protection; etching removes copper or other material. Exposure and development conditions depend on materials and methods, so do not apply one sequence to all boards.
Another method forms the required pattern by plating. In either case, inspect broken tracks, unwanted connections between neighboring patterns, dimensions, holes, and surfaces against process criteria. Board manufacture and later component mounting require separate control.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish process defects
paragraphs.text: If neighboring copper patterns are connected on an unpopulated board, identify it as a pattern-formation issue before soldering. A solder bridge between terminals after mounting is a different condition and discovery stage. Even with the same suspicion of a short, record location, process, material, and observed facts rather than deciding the cause in advance.

terms.meaning: A conducting path formed on a board.
Attaching electronic components to a board.
A protective film for areas to be retained during processing.
Processing that removes unwanted material using chemicals or another specified method.

mfg1-electrical-l026.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, process comparison 7 min, writing 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Compare unpopulated and populated boards and state the roles of conductor pattern, base, and components. Describe in words “protect required copper, remove unwanted copper.” Write separate reports for a copper connection and a solder bridge.
Self-check: Do you distinguish pattern formation from mounting and protective film from the copper being removed?
safety: Do not operate chemical, UV, or plating equipment from this explanation alone. Follow assigned procedures for ventilation, PPE, and waste liquids.
Do not bend flexible boards beyond specification or scrape away suspected defects without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l026.summary: Board manufacture and component assembly are different processes. Separate retained conductors, removed conductors, and protective-film functions.

mfg1-electrical-l027.title: Check grease functions and lubrication conditions
mfg1-electrical-l027.objective: Explain reduction of friction and wear and match specified grease, quantity, and application point.

paragraphs.title: Why grease is used
paragraphs.text:
Grease is a semisolid lubricant used in bearings and other moving contact surfaces. Lubrication reduces friction and wear; applying just any substance does not produce the same effect. The material must suit the location and operating conditions.
Documents may specify grease consistency. A measured penetration value and a product grade number do not necessarily use the same scale or numerical relationship, so do not judge suitability from a number’s size alone. Match the specified part number and the exact specification field.

paragraphs.title: More is not necessarily better
paragraphs.text:
Equipment procedures specify points, amount, interval, and application method. Too much, too little, or foreign matter can affect function. Use clean specified tools and check component condition and records. Do not mix different greases by visual similarity or color.
Similarly named products may serve mechanical lubrication, electrical contacts, or heat transfer. This lesson on mechanical lubrication does not authorize applying any grease to electronic components. Also confirm who is assigned and the required stopping conditions.

paragraphs.title: Example of unidentified material
paragraphs.text: A bearing-grease container has an unreadable label, while the previous record specifies product G-A. Do not add similarly colored G-B. Hold use and confirm material identity. Once the correct material and tools are confirmed, the assigned person applies the specified amount and records it. If there is unusual noise, do not assume lubrication will necessarily fix it.

terms.meaning: Supplying material to reduce friction or wear at contacting surfaces.
An effect opposing movement of contacting surfaces.
Surface loss caused by contact or motion.
Supplying grease to a specified location.

mfg1-electrical-l027.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, unidentified-material example 7 min, lubrication checklist 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Tabulate equipment number, material code, location, quantity, interval, and stopping conditions to check before greasing. Write a Japanese request for clarification about unlabeled grease. Explain why “more is better” is not valid.
Self-check: Do you avoid substitution by color and guessing unknown specifications?
safety: Do not reach into operating hazards to grease equipment; follow approved methods and isolation conditions.
Do not mix unidentified greases or apply lubricant to electrical terminals without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l027.summary: Match grease to its purpose and specifications. Confirm material, location, amount, interval, and stopping conditions.

mfg1-electrical-l028.title: Trace starting and stopping in a self-hold circuit
mfg1-electrical-l028.objective: Explain relay self-holding through state changes and distinguish start, hold, stop, and loss of power.

paragraphs.title: While pressed and after release
paragraphs.text:
In a basic teaching circuit, pressing a start a/NO contact energizes the relay coil and closes its own a/NO contact. Placing this auxiliary contact in parallel with the start contact leaves a path to the coil after the button is released. Continued energization through that path is self-holding.
A lamp remaining on does not necessarily mean the button is still pressed. Trace the contacts that complete the current path. Distinguish the initial open auxiliary contact from its energized state.

paragraphs.title: Stop and loss of power
paragraphs.text:
This example places a stop b/NC contact in series with the path. Stop operation opens it, de-energizes the coil, and returns the auxiliary contact, releasing the hold. This differs from a circuit that stops merely when the start button is released.
In the basic example with an ordinary non-latching relay and a released start input, losing power releases the hold, and restoration alone does not restart it. This is not an unconditional guarantee for real equipment: check circuit configuration, input states, and holding method.

paragraphs.title: Build a state table
paragraphs.text: Record: initially coil off/lamp off; after start coil on/lamp on; after start release still on through the auxiliary contact; after stop off. Add separate rows for power loss and restoration. Explain states using an approved drawing or teaching setup rather than experimenting on real machinery. Adequacy of stop and safety functions requires separate verification.

terms.meaning: Continuing operation by using a device’s own contact.
Passing current through a coil to create magnetism.
The reference condition before operation begins.
Ending a maintained state.

mfg1-electrical-l028.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, path tracing 7 min, state table 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Tabulate initial, starting, start-released, stopped, and power-lost states. Explain in Japanese which contact maintains the hold and which releases it. State the assumptions behind no restart from restoration alone.
Self-check: Have you stated ordinary non-latching relay and released start input without generalizing to real equipment?
safety: Do not bypass a stop contact or safety function to test self-holding.
Power-loss, restoration, and restart tests on real equipment are for assigned personnel under approved procedures and hazardous-area checks.
mfg1-electrical-l028.summary: Self-holding continues through a contact path. Trace stop, power loss, and restoration separately with assumptions stated.

mfg1-electrical-l029.title: Motor types and control purposes
mfg1-electrical-l029.objective: Explain electrical-to-rotation conversion and distinguish motor types from servo-control goals.

paragraphs.title: Energy and types
paragraphs.text:
A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation. There are DC and AC types; AC types include induction and synchronous motors. Equal voltage markings do not establish identical supply type, frequency, or connection.
Induction motors include squirrel-cage and wound-rotor types. Do not equate rotating-field speed with actual rotor speed. This lesson avoids memorizing a speed formula as actual RPM and instead emphasizes checking ratings, operating conditions, and control method.

paragraphs.title: What servo control matches
paragraphs.text:
Servo control can stop at a specified position, match a speed, or control turning torque. Feedback returns detected results from devices such as encoders to correct the difference from a command.
Simply rotating is not sufficient for a positioning system. Distinguish whether position, speed, or force must be met. Changing mounting or control settings can change machine behavior even with the same motor.

paragraphs.title: Organize requirements
paragraphs.text: Moving a conveyor at constant speed differs from stopping a table at a set location. Focus on speed for the first and position for the second while also checking torque and load conditions. Do not respond to a position error by merely raising speed; report command, detection, and mechanical observations within your role.

terms.meaning: A device converting electrical energy to mechanical motion.
The rotating part of a motor.
The turning action applied to a shaft.
Moving to and stopping at a specified position.

mfg1-electrical-l029.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, requirement comparison 7 min, specification checks 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Match constant-speed conveying, stopping at a specified position, and constant winding force to speed, position, and torque control. Make a motor-replacement checklist for supply type, ratings, mounting, detection, and control.
Self-check: Do you avoid assuming rotation alone satisfies requirements or confusing rotating-field and rotor speed?
safety: Do not touch rotating shafts or couplings; follow isolation procedures when removing covers.
Do not change phases or settings to test direction or speed without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l029.summary: Match motor supply, type, and ratings. Separate position, speed, torque, and detection requirements.

mfg1-electrical-l030.title: Transformer turns ratios and losses
mfg1-electrical-l030.objective: Calculate a basic AC transformer turns ratio and explain losses without load.

paragraphs.title: The relationship between windings
paragraphs.text:
A common transformer uses a core and multiple windings to change voltage through changing magnetic flux. For an ideal AC transformer, voltage ratio corresponds to turns ratio: V2/V1 = N2/N1.
Fewer secondary turns step voltage down; more step it up. Primary does not always mean high-voltage side. Nor can an ordinary AC transformer be used identically by applying DC directly. Check frequency, capacity, connections, and voltage rating.

paragraphs.title: No load does not mean no loss
paragraphs.text:
Even without a secondary load, applying primary voltage causes losses such as core loss. Current through winding resistance also causes copper loss. No secondary load does not mean the primary is safe or consumes no power.
The ideal ratio omits actual losses and voltage variation. A matching voltage does not allow unlimited load; remain within capacity, temperature, and other limits. Match insulation type and construction to the application too.

paragraphs.title: Turns-ratio example
paragraphs.text: For a calculation example, V1 = 100 V, N1 = 500 turns, N2 = 100 turns gives V2 = 100 × 100/500 = 20 V. This is an ideal-ratio value, not a wiring instruction. Check actual ratings and destinations on the nameplate and drawings. A lower secondary voltage does not remove primary-side danger.

terms.meaning: The winding side treated as receiving power.
The winding side treated as delivering power to the load.
Loss occurring in the core.
Loss caused by winding resistance.

mfg1-electrical-l030.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, turns ratio 7 min, loss comparison 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Find V2 for an ideal AC transformer with V1 = 120 V, N1 = 600 turns, N2 = 150 turns. Organize losses at no load and under load and explain why capacity checks are necessary.
Self-check: Do you obtain 30 V without claiming an unloaded primary is unenergized or lossless?
safety: Do not connect teaching materials or unidentified windings to household power based on a ratio calculation.
Follow assigned isolation and verification procedures covering both sides; do not judge safety from the low-voltage side alone.
mfg1-electrical-l030.summary: Use turns ratios under ideal AC assumptions. Check conversion, losses, capacity, and safety separately.

mfg1-electrical-l031.title: Circuit-breaker roles and abnormality response
mfg1-electrical-l031.objective: Distinguish breakers, load switches, and disconnectors and avoid unauthorized resetting.

paragraphs.title: Opening does not mean identical capability
paragraphs.text:
A circuit breaker interrupts load or short-circuit current within its ratings and application. Interrupting large current can create an arc between contacts, making arc extinction important. Having a contact-opening mechanism does not by itself mean fault current can be safely interrupted.
In this teaching distinction, load switches handle load current, while disconnectors isolate a circuit with no current flowing. Do not group all devices as “switches”; identify function from nameplates, drawings, and operating procedures.

paragraphs.title: Check what is protected and under what conditions
paragraphs.text:
A wiring circuit breaker protects wiring against overcurrent from overloads or short circuits. Its presence does not establish protection of people against every leakage or shock condition. Check required protective functions and selection conditions for the equipment.
After a breaker operates, check the stopped area and people’s safety and report abnormality information. Repeatedly resetting without knowing the cause may worsen a fault or cause danger from restarting.

paragraphs.title: Example record after a trip
paragraphs.text: If a breaker trips during operation and there is a burnt smell, follow stop, evacuation, and reporting procedures instead of resetting to investigate. Record equipment number, time, operating state, indications, and smell. Do not substitute a different device, such as trying to interrupt fault current by opening a disconnector.

terms.meaning: A device interrupting load or fault current within its ratings.
An unintended low-resistance path.
Extinguishing an electrical arc.
A device isolating a circuit with no current flowing.

mfg1-electrical-l031.activity:
Approximate 30-minute plan: review 3 min, reading 10 min, device comparison 7 min, abnormality report 7 min, summary 3 min.
Writing: Tabulate which currents breakers, load switches, and disconnectors handle in the teaching distinction. Write a Japanese report about a burnt smell and stoppage and explain why not to reset without authorization.
Self-check: Do you distinguish device roles and ratings and avoid equating wiring protection with all electric-shock protection?
safety: Do not experiment with short circuits or interruption on real equipment. High-voltage operation requires qualifications, training, and approved procedures.
Do not repeatedly reset an unexplained trip or increase a rating without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l031.summary: Devices differ in the currents they can interrupt and their applications. After operation, prioritize cause checks and safe restoration.

mfg1-electrical-l032.title: Separate solar-cell and storage-battery roles
