Angles, however, use degrees or other angular units, so the same number can have a different meaning. Check the drawing’s unit specification first. If different dimensions are given for the same feature, do not choose whichever suits you; identify the conflicting area and ask for clarification.

terms.meaning: A line that indicates a dimension and has end marks.
A line that helps identify the positions to which a dimension applies.
The dimension required after machining or other processing is complete.
A dimension repeated for the same feature.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-046.activity:
4 min: Review the terms and learning objective.
10 min: Read the text and organize the relationship between drawing instructions and work.
7 min: Write your judgment for a concrete situation and the points still unconfirmed.
7 min: Draw a rectangular plate, distinguishing dimension lines from extension lines. Record length 24 and angle 24° in separate columns, and write an inquiry note for a situation where different values are given for the same feature.
2 min: Summarize the key points and what you want to confirm at work.
safety: Do not resolve contradictory duplicate dimensions by shop-floor judgment alone. Do not continue machining before the approved requirement is confirmed.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-046.summary: Read the value, unit and feature as one set. Check the line roles and finished condition, and ask about conflicts.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-047.title: Connect detail and reference dimensions to machining information
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-047.objective: Distinguish radius, diameter, thickness and hole-machining instructions from reference dimensions in parentheses.

paragraphs.title: Read the symbol together with the feature
paragraphs.text: Radius is indicated by R, diameter by φ, and plate thickness by t, for example. Symbols may sometimes be omitted when the dimension-line direction or end marks make the meaning clear. Do not decide the dimension type solely because a symbol is not visible; check the feature and both ends of the dimension line. For example, R6 means radius 6 and φ6 means diameter 6; they do not specify the same shape.

paragraphs.title: Check machining conditions as well as hole diameter
paragraphs.text: When different hole-making methods need to be distinguished, the nominal tool size and machining method are also specified. Do not treat a drilled hole and a finishing reaming operation as the same process simply because their nominal diameters match. A through hole may be shown without a depth dimension, but the absence of a visible depth alone does not prove that every hole is through; compare the other views and instructions.

paragraphs.title: Keep the meaning of the parentheses
paragraphs.text: A reference dimension is a value provided for reference, with its number in parentheses. It may show a value obtainable from other dimensions. Omitting the parentheses when copying can change the understood role of the dimension. Do not independently substitute a parenthesized value as the sole basis for machining or acceptance; check the underlying instructions and inspection plan.

terms.meaning: The distance from a circle’s centre to its circumference.
The thickness of a plate.
A hole that passes all the way through a component.
A dimension given in parentheses for reference.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-047.activity:
4 min: Review the terms and learning objective.
10 min: Read the text and organize the relationship between drawing instructions and work.
7 min: Write your judgment for a concrete situation and the points still unconfirmed.
7 min: Copy R8, φ8, t2.0 and (18), recording their respective roles. Separate the checks for drilling and reaming, and list the views to consult and questions to ask if the hole depth is unclear.
2 min: Summarize the key points and what you want to confirm at work.
safety: Do not machine a hole on your own judgment when its depth or machining method is unclear. Do not replace official inspection conditions with reference dimensions without authorization.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-047.summary: Read detail symbols and machining methods, and preserve reference-dimension parentheses. Check the whole drawing for missing instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-048.title: Check the feature and datum of a geometrical tolerance
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-048.objective: Distinguish shape, orientation and other requirements that dimensions alone cannot fully express, and the datum used as a reference.

paragraphs.title: A dimension range does not tell you every requirement
paragraphs.text: Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

paragraphs.title: Read the frame in order and trace the feature
paragraphs.text: A geometrical-tolerance frame gives the characteristic symbol, tolerance value and datum references where needed. For a paper example saying “parallelism, 0.08, B,” read not only 0.08 but also what must be parallel to reference B. Also check, through details such as the arrow attachment position, whether it applies to a surface or an axis.

paragraphs.title: Do not substitute your own reference
paragraphs.text: A datum is a reference used when considering a geometrical tolerance. The attachment position on the drawing may differ for surface and axis indications. Do not add an unnecessary reference to a characteristic such as flatness, which concerns form on its own. If the reference surface or axis cannot be identified, do not finalize the measuring method; ask the person responsible about the feature, reference and applicable standard.

terms.meaning: An indication specifying allowable variation in form, orientation, position and similar characteristics.
A geometrical characteristic relating to how flat a surface is.
A geometrical characteristic relating to parallelism relative to a reference.
A reference used when considering geometrical tolerances.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-048.activity:
4 min: Review the terms and learning objective.
10 min: Read the text and organize the relationship between drawing instructions and work.
7 min: Write your judgment for a concrete situation and the points still unconfirmed.
7 min: Put length, flatness and parallelism requirements in separate columns. For the paper example “parallelism 0.08, reference B,” identify the feature and reference, and write a measurement inquiry for an unclear feature.
2 min: Summarize the key points and what you want to confirm at work.
safety: Do not accept a geometrical tolerance using a convenient nearby surface as a reference when the specified reference or feature is unconfirmed. Measure by an approved method.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-048.summary: Treat the characteristic, value, feature and required reference as a set. A dimensional measurement alone is no substitute.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-049.title: Trace the features specified by surface-texture and welding symbols
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-049.objective: Separate surface-texture parameters from weld type, position and edge-preparation instructions when asking for clarification.

paragraphs.title: Do not extract only the surface-texture number
paragraphs.text: Surface condition affects machine performance and includes waviness and roughness. Drawings add a parameter such as Ra or Rz and its value to a symbol, indicating the relevant surface directly or with a leader line. The same number means something different with a different parameter. Do not reuse a value from another surface; also check the machining-related symbol, relevant surface and measurement conditions.

paragraphs.title: Separate weld type from weld position
paragraphs.text: A welding symbol is built around a reference line and basic symbol, with necessary dimensions and supplementary instructions added. Basic symbols distinguish square, V and single-bevel groove welds, fillet welds and other types. In the notation shown in this textbook, a basic symbol below the reference line indicates the arrow side, and one above it indicates the other side. On an actual drawing, also confirm the applicable standard and notation system; do not turn the drawing over and decide the position yourself.

paragraphs.title: Check which component needs edge preparation and the supplementary instructions
paragraphs.text: Edge preparation is the form made at a component’s end for welding. A bent arrow may indicate which component is to receive the preparation, but an unbent arrow may be used when the component is already clear, for example. Do not decide which side to machine solely from whether the arrow is bent; check the basic symbol, component, dimensions and supplementary instructions together. Reading symbols does not authorize you to omit work qualifications or safety procedures.

terms.reading: ひょうめんせいじょう
terms.meaning: Surface condition, including roughness and waviness.
A line linking a symbol or explanation to the relevant feature.
The reference line on which basic welding symbols and other information are placed.
The shape prepared at the end of a component for welding.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-049.activity:
4 min: Review the terms and learning objective.
10 min: Read the text and organize the relationship between drawing instructions and work.
7 min: Write your judgment for a concrete situation and the points still unconfirmed.
7 min: Copy the Ra and Rz specifications of two surfaces into separate columns. Using the textbook’s notation, describe in words the difference between arrow-side and other-side welding. Write an inquiry note if it is unclear which component needs edge preparation.
2 min: Summarize the key points and what you want to confirm at work.
safety: Do not machine while the weld position or edge-preparation shape is unclear. Actual work must meet prescribed safety conditions, including qualifications and training, fire prevention and protective equipment.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-049.summary: For surface texture, check the parameter and surface; for welding, check the type and position. Do not omit the applicable standard or supplementary instructions.

mfg1-electrical-l036.title: Check screw/tool compatibility and tightening conditions
mfg1-electrical-l036.objective: Select tools matching the screw head and nominal dimensions, and explain assembly conditions without confusing torque with component specifications.

paragraphs.title: Do not substitute tools merely because they look similar
paragraphs.text: Use a slotted screwdriver matching the slot width for slotted screws and a suitable cross-head driver for cross recesses. Use a hex key for hex-socket bolts and a suitable spanner or ring spanner matching the width across flats for hex bolts and nuts. The nominal thread diameter and the width across flats do not necessarily have the same value. If a tool is loose, do not keep pressing it harder; check size and wear.

paragraphs.title: Follow the torque specification
paragraphs.text: A torque wrench controls the specified tightening torque. Do not choose settings from bolt appearance or operator strength alone. Check the component, unit, setting and tightening sequence against drawings and work standards. Tighter is not always better: both insufficient and excessive tightening cause problems. Check the management status of tools requiring calibration or pre-use checks.

paragraphs.title: Check washers and screw types
paragraphs.text: Plain washers, spring washers and screws with captive washers have different configurations. Do not substitute types indiscriminately or omit specified washers. Self-tapping screws form an internal thread as they are driven into an appropriate pilot hole; this does not mean they suit every material or hole. If specified parts are missing, report the part number and shortage for confirmation.

terms.meaning: The distance between opposing flat faces of a hexagonal section.
The magnitude of the turning action used to tighten a screw or similar fastener.
A flat washer used in a threaded joint.
A screw that forms its own internal thread in a suitable pilot hole.

mfg1-electrical-l036.activity:
30-minute guide: review3min, text9min, tool matching table8min, assembly-error study7min, summary3min.
Writing: Name suitable tools for slotted, cross-recess, hex-socket and hex-nut fasteners. Explain nominal diameter versus width across flats and list four checks before torque-controlled work. Write a report for missing specified washers.
Self-check: Can you check tool fit, component specifications and tightening conditions separately?
safety: Do not force damaged screws or tools into use. Confirm prescribed power isolation before working inside electrical equipment.
Do not add unauthorized leverage such as extension bars. Follow torque-wrench instructions and specified limits.
mfg1-electrical-l036.summary: Check screw heads, width across flats, washers and tightening conditions. Confirm specified torque rather than deciding from appearance or brute force.

mfg1-electrical-l037.title: Choose chassis-working tools by their purpose
mfg1-electrical-l037.objective: Distinguish marking, hole-centre marking, cutting and threading tools, and explain layout checks before machining.

paragraphs.title: Locate features before making shapes
paragraphs.text: A chassis supports equipment components. A scriber marks dimensions and positions on metal; a punch makes an indentation at a hole centre. For layouts that may change, do not immediately scratch permanent lines: make temporary marks by the appropriate procedure and check them. Align reference surfaces and orientation, then confirm components will fit before proceeding.

paragraphs.title: Cutting, drilling and threading
paragraphs.text: Drills make holes and pilot holes for tapping; hole saws make relatively large mounting holes. Taps cut internal threads and dies cut external threads. End mills operate in milling machines and cut with peripheral or end cutting edges. Even tools described as cutting tools differ in compatible material, shape, machine and required dimensions.

paragraphs.title: Work continues after cutting
paragraphs.text: When cutting metal with a hacksaw and hand-finishing with a file, check remaining burrs and interference with parts as well as the cut face. Burrs are protrusions created by cutting or drilling metal and other materials and can cause injury or assembly faults. Before machining, prepare tools, clamping and chip collection, and avoid using tools outside their intended purpose.

terms.meaning: Marking machining dimensions or hole positions on a workpiece.
A tool that indents hole centres and similar positions.
A tool for cutting internal threads.
A tool for cutting external threads.

mfg1-electrical-l037.activity:
30-minute guide: text10min, tool classification7min, operation sequence8min, explanation5min.
Writing: Classify scribers, punches, drills, taps, dies and files by use. Write the check sequence for preventing incorrect hole locations in a control panel. Explain two ways burrs affect subsequent assembly.
Self-check: Can you distinguish internal- and external-thread tools and check locations before cutting?
safety: Clamp the workpiece appropriately and avoid injury from sharp scribers, cut faces and chips.
Follow authorized rotating-tool safety procedures. Do not remove chips with hands or tools while rotation continues.
mfg1-electrical-l037.summary: Choose tools by workpiece and purpose. Treat location checks, machining and burr checks as one continuous process.

mfg1-electrical-l038.title: Align references for comparison and height measurement
mfg1-electrical-l038.objective: Distinguish dial indicators, height gauges, rules and surface plates, and explain references and readings.

paragraphs.title: Detect changes with a dial indicator
paragraphs.text: A dial indicator mechanically magnifies small probe movements and displays them with a pointer. It is used for runout, flatness and dimensional comparison. Check the division and full-revolution values for the model; do not infer an absolute dimension solely from pointer motion. After setting the reference, compare under the same contact conditions and record both direction and amount of pointer movement.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish height from depth
paragraphs.text: A height gauge measures or marks heights from a reference surface. A reading mechanism resembling a vernier caliper does not give it every caliper function. Do not universally treat it as a hole-depth instrument: choose an instrument suited to the intended dimension. Dirt on the reference or base changes the measuring posture, so check before use.

paragraphs.title: Surface plates and end faces
paragraphs.text: A surface plate supplies a reference plane for measurement or assembly; it does not itself display dimensions. Some metal rules use the graduated end as their starting point. Distinguish this from reading a caliper reference line, and check wear, dirt, positioning and required measurement accuracy.

terms.meaning: Measurement examining differences or changes relative to a reference.
The part that contacts the workpiece and transmits displacement or similar movement.
An instrument for measuring or marking height from a reference plane.
A table supplying a reference plane for measurement or assembly.

mfg1-electrical-l038.activity:
30-minute guide: text10min, instrument selection7min, references and readings8min, summary5min.
Writing: Choose instruments for shaft runout, height above a reference, hole depth and approximate length, with reasons. Assuming a dial division of0.01mm, calculate a difference of four divisions. Explain how dirt on a surface plate affects measurement.
Self-check: Are you mistakenly treating minimum graduations as a guarantee of actual measurement accuracy?
safety: Do not drop instruments or force the probe inward.
Measure rotating objects only by an approved safe method; do not move machinery carelessly.
mfg1-electrical-l038.summary: Comparison, height and length use different references. Check surface plates, end faces and reference positions, then measure dimensions suited to the instrument.

mfg1-electrical-l039.title: Check the quantities and conditions measured by electrical instruments
mfg1-electrical-l039.objective: Classify LCR meters, thermocouples, lux meters and gaussmeters by measured quantity and explain condition checks.

paragraphs.title: Measuring component values with an LCR meter
paragraphs.text: An LCR meter measures coil inductance L, capacitor capacitance C, resistance R, impedance and related quantities. Its targets and methods differ from a tester reading resistance or voltage. Check component type, connection, test frequency and other conditions against specifications rather than judging acceptance from a number alone. Whether a component can remain connected to a circuit also depends on the instrument and procedure.

paragraphs.title: Thermocouples use temperature difference
paragraphs.text: A thermocouple combines different metals and uses thermoelectric voltage arising from a junction temperature difference. Reference-junction treatment matters as well as the temperature at the measurement side. Check agreement of type, compensating leads, polarity and instrument setting. Do not guarantee an operating range from thermocouple type alone: judge it from product specifications and operating conditions.

paragraphs.title: Light and magnetic field are different quantities
paragraphs.text: A lux meter measures illuminance related to light reaching its receiver; a gaussmeter measures magnetic flux density using a Hall element or similar sensor. Bright light and a strong magnetic field are different evaluations. Sensor orientation, location and outside influences affect results, so match conditions for comparisons. Record both the unit and instrument name to prevent mix-ups.

terms.meaning: A quantity describing properties associated with current changes in coils and similar components.
A temperature sensor using thermoelectric voltage from dissimilar metals and junction temperature differences.
A quantity expressing the amount of light reaching a surface.
One quantity describing the state of a magnetic field.

mfg1-electrical-l039.activity:
30-minute guide: text10min, quantity matching7min, condition comparison8min, explanation5min.
Writing: Match L/C/R, temperature, illuminance and magnetic flux density with instruments. List three checks when replacing a thermocouple. Explain why readings of the same product from different positions cannot simply be compared.
Self-check: Do you check sensor type and conditions rather than generalizing one temperature range to every product?
safety: For energized measurements or residual capacitor charge, follow instrument specifications and approved isolation and discharge procedures.
Do not touch hot areas. Observe sensor and compensating-lead heat-resistance limits.
mfg1-electrical-l039.summary: Select instruments for the quantity and record units, connections and sensor conditions. Check thermocouple operating ranges in product specifications.

mfg1-electrical-l040.title: Follow preparations for drilling and tapping in order
mfg1-electrical-l040.objective: Separate reference-based positioning, pilot drilling, threading and deburring, and explain when not to force a tool.

paragraphs.title: Check centres before machining
paragraphs.text: Measure mounting-hole locations from the specified reference surface. Temporarily mark centre lines and outlines, place the actual device to check interference and orientation, then use a punch or other prescribed method. A hole made at the wrong location is not easily undone. Enlarge large holes in stages from a pilot hole as needed and clamp the workpiece securely.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish pilot holes from internal threads
paragraphs.text: Tapping forms an internal thread inside a pilot hole. The pilot diameter is not simply the nominal thread diameter: check tables matching the specified thread diameter, pitch, material and machining method. Follow the procedure for centre drilling, pilot drilling, chamfering, cutting-fluid use and other required preparations. Do not apply one hole diameter to every material based only on an approximate ratio in a reference.

paragraphs.title: Alignment and chip handling
paragraphs.text: Hold a hand tap in a tap wrench and maintain the proper orientation to the workpiece. Handle chips in the order and manner suited to the tool type. Do not force the tap through if resistance suddenly increases. Check pilot hole, tool, lubrication and chips to prevent breakage or defective threads. Afterwards inspect burrs and threads and keep chips out of equipment.

terms.meaning: A hole drilled in advance for a later machining operation.
A thread formed inside a hole.
Machining an edge or hole rim to the specified shape.
A tool for holding and turning a tap by hand.

mfg1-electrical-l040.activity:
30-minute guide: text10min, process cards8min, fault study7min, summary5min.
Writing: Divide positioning through burr checks into six stages. List three conditions for selecting a pilot diameter. Write a stop-and-check report for a hand tap that becomes hard to turn.
Self-check: Can you distinguish nominal thread diameter from pilot diameter and avoid excessive leverage?
safety: Do not arbitrarily mount a hand tap in a rotating drill chuck. Follow approved equipment and tool methods.
Do not machine while holding the workpiece by hand. Remove chips safely after rotation stops.
mfg1-electrical-l040.summary: Check positions and pilot-hole conditions before machining. If a tap becomes hard to turn, investigate rather than forcing it.

mfg1-electrical-l041.title: Select file cross-sections and cutting directions
mfg1-electrical-l041.objective: Choose a file suited to the shape and explain forward-stroke cutting and checks during detailed finishing.

paragraphs.title: Match cross-section to the intended shape
paragraphs.text: Metalworking files cut and abrade metal by hand and come in flat, half-round, round, square, triangular and other shapes. Flat faces, round holes, curves, grooves and sharp corners present different contact surfaces. Do not select a tool merely because it fits: distinguish the surface to remove from surfaces to retain. Half-round files provide both flat and curved working surfaces.

paragraphs.title: Cut on the push stroke
paragraphs.text: Ordinary metalworking file teeth are arranged to cut when pushed forward. Instead of equal pressure in both directions, apply suitable pressure forward and release it on return. Clamping, handle condition and clogged teeth also affect results. Check dimensions during work to avoid removing too much.

paragraphs.title: Use small file sets for details
paragraphs.text: Needle-file sets combine small files for detailed hand finishing. Their various sections suit confined areas and fine features. Do not force a large file into a narrow space and damage surrounding areas; finish only the necessary area gradually. When deburring drilled or cut features, check effects on assembly and specified dimensions rather than stopping at appearance alone.

terms.meaning: A file used for hand-finishing metal and similar work.
A file cross-section with both flat and curved surfaces.
A set of small files used for detailed finishing.
A condition in which chips or other matter clog the spaces between cutting teeth.

mfg1-electrical-l041.activity:
30-minute guide: text9min, section selection7min, movement explanation7min, finishing plan7min.
Writing: Choose shapes for flat faces, round holes, curves and narrow corners, with reasons. Explain pressure on forward and return strokes. List four checks before and after deburring a mounting hole.
Self-check: Can you distinguish deburring from hole enlargement and check for excessive removal during work?
safety: Check for damaged or loose handles and watch file tips and sharp workpiece edges.
Do not brush chips away directly by hand. Use specified cleaning tools and protection.
mfg1-electrical-l041.summary: Choose the section and size for the surface and follow forward-stroke cutting. Continue checking dimensions and surfaces to retain.

mfg1-electrical-l042.title: Organize charge, magnetic fields and Fleming’s rules
mfg1-electrical-l042.objective: Distinguish forces between charges, current/field relationships and the uses of the left- and right-hand rules.

paragraphs.title: Charge signs and separation
paragraphs.text: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. In an ideal point-charge model, force magnitude is proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to separation squared. With unchanged charges and medium, doubling separation reduces force magnitude to one quarter. Signs help determine direction; explain magnitude and direction separately.

paragraphs.title: Fields and forces produced by current
paragraphs.text: Electric current, as well as magnets, creates a magnetic field. In an idealized pair of parallel conductors, currents in the same direction attract and opposite currents repel. Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field depends on field and current directions. Do not treat current, field and mechanical force as one quantity: draw their arrows separately.

paragraphs.title: Left hand for force; right hand for induction
paragraphs.text: Fleming’s left-hand rule gives the force direction on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field: thumb for force, first finger for field and middle finger for current. The right-hand rule gives induced electromotive-force direction when a conductor moves in a field: thumb for motion, first finger for field and middle finger for induced electromotive force. With a closed circuit it also helps determine induced-current direction. Rather than memorizing merely opposite hands, distinguish given conditions from the quantity sought.

terms.meaning: A property or quantity responsible for electrical forces.
The condition of space used to describe magnetic effects.

terms.reading: ゆうどうきでんりょく
terms.meaning: Electromotive force generated by electromagnetic induction.
A relationship in which one quantity decreases as the other increases while their product remains constant.

mfg1-electrical-l042.activity:
30-minute guide: text10min, arrows8min, ratio calculation7min, explanation5min.
Writing: Explain forces between like and unlike charges. Calculate the force ratio when point-charge separation triples under unchanged conditions. Tabulate the two given conditions and sought quantity for each hand rule. Explain why circuit conditions matter when calling the right middle finger the current direction.
Self-check: Can you distinguish current, field, force, motion and induced electromotive force?
safety: Study with diagrams or cards; do not put hands into energized equipment to test the rules.
Electromagnetic forces can move parts. Actual equipment tests require authorized equipment and protective procedures.
mfg1-electrical-l042.summary: Distinguish charge forces from magnetic-field forces. The left hand concerns force from current; the right hand concerns induced electromotive force from motion.

mfg1-surface-lesson-036.title: Prevent mix-ups through reporting, communication, consultation and 5S
mfg1-surface-lesson-036.objective:
Use reporting, communication and consultation to suit the situation.
Connect 5S and the three fixed rules to chemical and jig management.

paragraphs.title: Separate facts from judgments
paragraphs.text:
Reporting conveys progress or results; communication shares necessary information with those concerned; consultation seeks advice on matters you cannot decide. When reporting a surface-treatment abnormality, state the conclusion first, followed by the process, time, affected lot and confirmed values.
Separate an assumption such as “I think the chemical is the cause” from an observation such as “The label is unreadable.” Check that the listener understood and repeat the instructions received.

paragraphs.title: Combine tidying with identification
paragraphs.text:
5S means sorting, setting in order, cleaning, maintaining cleanliness and discipline. Separate unnecessary items from necessary ones, decide how to arrange necessary items, remove dirt, and maintain that condition and the rules. Even if a chemical container seems unnecessary, do not discard it without the prescribed decision.
If cleaning reveals an abnormality, do not merely remove the dirt and finish. Record the location and possible leak, keep away from the hazardous area and notify the responsible person.

paragraphs.title: Make storage clear to everyone with the three fixed rules
paragraphs.text:
The three fixed rules specify location, item and quantity. A designated shelf alone does not establish control if its contents or quantity are wrong. Compare the label with the actual item and restore the specified condition after use.
Do not distinguish similar containers or jigs by color alone; check names, identification numbers and suitability for the process. Substituting another item without permission can affect both quality and safety.

paragraphs.title: Shift handover
paragraphs.text: A jig from another process was mixed into the cleaning-jig shelf. Record its number and location, identify it using the prescribed hold method and consult the responsible person. Tell the next operator it is under review. Do not discard it as part of sorting or move it to an empty shelf where it becomes harder to trace.

terms.meaning: Information sharing through reporting, communication and consultation.
Deciding where items are placed.
Deciding which item belongs in a location.
Setting and controlling the quantity kept.

mfg1-surface-lesson-036.activity:
Write a report about mixed jigs in the order: conclusion, observed facts, request.
Explain one example of each of the three fixed rules for your tool storage.
safety: Do not open an unknown container or pour its contents into a drain because you consider them unnecessary.
Cleaning a hazardous leak requires instructions from a trained, authorized person.
mfg1-surface-lesson-036.summary:
Communicate specific facts through reporting, communication and consultation.
Maintain 5S and verify location, item and quantity to prevent mix-ups.

mfg1-surface-lesson-037.title: Record 4M changes and verify improvements with PDCA
mfg1-surface-lesson-037.objective:
Distinguish QCDS from 4M.
Use on-site facts and PDCA to check improvement results.

paragraphs.title: Do not focus on quality alone
paragraphs.text:
QCD stands for quality, cost and delivery; QCDS adds safety. Faster, cheaper processing is not a good improvement if it fails performance requirements or increases danger.
Define the improvement goal with numbers or observable conditions, and decide first what must be maintained. Do not skip inspections or safety procedures to meet a deadline.

paragraphs.title: 4M and facts at the workplace
paragraphs.text:
4M means people, machinery/equipment, materials and methods. When defects increase, arrange changes such as operator handovers, equipment checks, material lots and treatment procedures in time order. A changed factor is a clue, not proof of the cause.
The three-actuals principle checks the actual place, actual item and actual facts. Compare records with real conditions and separate observations from hypotheses. Checking the actual item does not authorize approaching hazardous equipment.

paragraphs.title: Keep an evaluation after implementation
paragraphs.text:
PDCA is a cycle of plan, do, check and act. Set goals and methods, implement within the approved scope and compare results under matching conditions. Feed the evaluation into the next plan or standard during the improvement stage.
Implementation alone does not demonstrate effectiveness. State differences in sample sizes or periods, and consider chance or other changes. Obtain the prescribed approval for changes.

paragraphs.title: Use comparable conditions
paragraphs.text: In a hypothetical record, 10 of 200 items were defective before action and 4 of 80 afterward. The count fell, but both defect rates are 5%. Record the denominator rather than concluding that the rate fell to less than half. This is a calculation exercise, not an acceptable defect rate for a real process.

terms.meaning: The four factors: people, machinery, materials and methods.
Checking facts through the actual place, actual item and actual facts.
The proportion of defective items among all items examined.
Checking results against goals and conditions.

mfg1-surface-lesson-037.activity:
For defects increasing after a shift change, list information to check under each 4M factor.
Calculate the example defect rates and write what additional information is needed to assess improvement.
safety: Do not skip safety procedures or inspections during quality improvement.
Follow the prescribed safety procedure when opening equipment for investigation.
mfg1-surface-lesson-037.summary:
A change is a possible cause, not proof.
PDCA retains the evaluation after implementation and the next improvement.

mfg1-surface-lesson-038.title: Distinguish work standards from QC process charts
mfg1-surface-lesson-038.objective:
Distinguish work procedures from process control plans.
Check control frequency and abnormality responses as well.

paragraphs.title: The purpose of standardization
paragraphs.text:
Standardization shares rules and criteria to reduce variation in work. Work standards specify procedures, equipment, tools and precautions. Even experienced workers must not assume another product type or a revised procedure is unchanged.
Before work, check the product, process, document number and revision. A legible document for another process is not a valid basis.

paragraphs.title: Read the control plan
paragraphs.text:
A QC process chart summarizes control items, methods, frequency, responsibilities and actions for abnormalities for each process. Read not only what to measure but also when, who checks it and what to do when a value is outside the limit.
Even if you understand coating-thickness measurement, using the wrong lot or timing may fail the control plan. Work standards and QC process charts complement each other with different information.

paragraphs.title: Do not fill gaps with your own method
paragraphs.text:
Ask for clarification when frequency or criteria cannot be read or two documents conflict. Do not rely only on memory or choose the more convenient criterion.
For abnormal values, take prescribed action and keep product identification and records. If a standard needs changing, submit reasons and findings through the prescribed process; operators must not rewrite it without permission.

paragraphs.title: A mismatch in measurement frequency
paragraphs.text: A hypothetical plan requires designated samples from every lot. A morning measurement does not authorize skipping a different afternoon lot. Even with a correct measurement method, check whether frequency and coverage are insufficient and consult the responsible person.

terms.meaning: Establishing common rules and criteria.

terms.reading: きゅーしーこうていず
terms.meaning: A document showing control items and methods for each process.
How often or at what intervals control is performed.
Reviewing content and updating its version.

mfg1-surface-lesson-038.activity:
List three items to check in work standards and three in a QC process chart.
Write a clarification request for conflicting documents.
safety: Do not change documents or inspection frequency without permission.
Prioritize abnormality responses and instructions to hold affected products.
mfg1-surface-lesson-038.summary:
Check the work method together with the control plan.
Do not overlook applicability, revision, frequency or abnormality responses.

mfg1-surface-lesson-039.title: Choose QC tools according to what you need to investigate
mfg1-surface-lesson-039.objective:
Explain differences between counts, distributions, time trends and relationships.
Do not determine causes or conformity from a graph alone.

paragraphs.title: Define categories before collecting data
paragraphs.text:
A check sheet records defect types and other data using consistent categories. Changing category names or counting methods between days makes comparison difficult. Avoid double counting and record the total examined, period and process.
A Pareto chart arranges items in descending order of count or another measure and shows the cumulative proportion. High-count items are candidates for investigation, but this is no reason to ignore rare, serious safety issues.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish distributions from time order
paragraphs.text:
A histogram groups values into intervals and displays counts to show spread and distribution shape. A control chart instead monitors time-ordered changes using control limits and other information. Remember that a histogram hides measurement order.
Control limits assess process variation; they do not mean the same thing as product specification limits. Points inside the lines do not prove that every product meets specifications.

paragraphs.title: Do not confuse relationships with causes
paragraphs.text:
A scatter diagram plots paired observations to examine a relationship. Seeing a relationship does not prove that one variable causes the other. Check other conditions and biases in the records.
A cause-and-effect diagram organizes possible factors behind a problem. Use 4M and other groupings to expand candidates, but factors on the diagram remain unverified hypotheses. Choose bar or line graphs according to the purpose as well.

paragraphs.title: Choose the method from the purpose
paragraphs.text: To examine treatment time and coating thickness, pair both values for each item in a scatter diagram. Consider a time-ordered graph for weekly counts and a Pareto chart for prioritizing defect types. Choose by the question to answer, not visual appeal.

terms.meaning: A recording sheet for collecting data under defined items.
The proportion of the total represented by successively accumulated quantities.
Boundaries used to assess process variation.
An association between changes in two variables.

mfg1-surface-lesson-039.activity:
Choose tools for four purposes: defect types, time trends, value distribution and the relationship between two variables.
Write two checks needed after a scatter diagram shows an association.
safety: Do not delete abnormal values to make graphs look better.
Do not postpone a serious safety issue solely because its count is small.
mfg1-surface-lesson-039.summary:
Each tool reveals different information.
Correlation does not prove causation, and control limits differ from specification limits.

mfg1-surface-lesson-040.title: Compare corrosion of iron, copper, aluminum and zinc
mfg1-surface-lesson-040.objective:
Explain how corrosion protection works and its limits for different metals.
Do not choose a treatment solely from a change in appearance.

paragraphs.title: Covering iron and the role of zinc
paragraphs.text:
Iron and steel corrode in environments involving moisture, oxygen and other factors. Blocking the environment with paint differs from protecting iron through preferential corrosion of zinc.
The zinc in zinc plating is itself consumed. Do not assume a coating provides permanent protection; check the environment, scratches, remaining coating and specification together.

paragraphs.title: Copper and aluminum surfaces
paragraphs.text:
Copper can form relatively stable surface films depending on the environment, but may discolor and can be affected by sulfides and other substances. “Copper withstands every chemical” is incorrect.
Aluminum’s natural oxide film protects its surface, but is thin and may be damaged by the environment or treatment. Do not regard it as having the same thickness or performance as an anodic oxide film produced by a controlled process.

paragraphs.title: Check the environment and specification
paragraphs.text:
Zinc can also be affected by corrosion under acidic, alkaline or other conditions. Confirm the post-treatment against required performance, material and applicable specification. Do not treat representative process names in this material as chemical recipes for workplace use.
If discoloration or rust is found, record material, position, storage conditions, wetting and lot. Authorized personnel decide conformity, reprocessing and chemical selection.

paragraphs.title: Explain differences in appearance
paragraphs.text: White deposits were found on a zinc coating over iron. Do not immediately conclude that white means harmless or that the iron must have red rust. Ask quality personnel to check coating condition and requirements. Do not merely polish away the appearance and proceed to shipping approval.

terms.meaning: Protection of one metal by preferential corrosion of another.
An oxide film formed naturally by reaction with air or other surroundings.
A change in surface color.
Conditions such as moisture and chemicals where a product is used.

mfg1-surface-lesson-040.activity:
Explain how paint covering iron differs from zinc corrosion protection.
For copper, aluminum and zinc, explain why corrosion resistance cannot be asserted without conditions.
safety: Do not touch corrosion products or residual liquids with bare hands.
Do not infer chemical mixtures or reprocessing instructions from treatment names in this material.
mfg1-surface-lesson-040.summary:
Consider metal, coating and environment together.
Zinc protects iron while itself corroding.

mfg1-surface-lesson-041.title: Use Ohm’s law with units and stated conditions
mfg1-surface-lesson-041.objective:
Calculate the relationship between voltage, current and resistance.
Convert mA and mV, and distinguish ideal-resistor calculations from real processes.

paragraphs.title: Write one relationship three ways
paragraphs.text:
For current I through resistance R and voltage E across it, E=RI, I=E/R and R=E/I. Units are volts V, amperes A and ohms Ω. Decide what to find first, then organize given values and units.
At constant resistance, increasing voltage increases current. At constant voltage, increasing resistance decreases current. Always state which quantity is held constant.

paragraphs.title: Align prefixes before calculating
paragraphs.text:
The prefix m means one thousandth. 200mA is 0.200A and 80mV is 0.080V. Entering numbers without units can create a thousandfold error. Convert to V and A first and include units such as Ω in the answer.
After rearranging a formula, check using the original relationship. If a calculated value disagrees with a measurement, check units, assumptions and the object’s condition; do not rewrite it to a convenient value.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish a resistor model from a plating tank
paragraphs.text:
These calculations assume a resistor for which Ohm’s law applies within the range considered. Electrode reactions, contacts and solution conditions also affect a plating tank’s power readings; the whole tank cannot always be treated as a constant resistance.
A change in voltage and current readings alone does not identify solution concentration or a single cause. Investigate prescribed monitoring items using equipment procedures. There is no need to change real equipment settings to study calculations.

paragraphs.title: Check with units
paragraphs.text: Suppose an ideal resistor carries 30mA at 120mV. Convert to E=0.120V and I=0.030A: R=0.120/0.030=4Ω. The check 4Ω×0.030A=0.120V returns the original value. These numbers are for paper exercises, not equipment settings.

terms.meaning: A difference in electric potential associated with driving current.
A quantity expressing opposition to current flow.
A symbol before a unit indicating a multiple or fraction.
Verifying an answer with another calculation or method.

mfg1-surface-lesson-041.activity:
Calculate current for an ideal 6Ω resistor at 18V on paper.
Find resistance from 60mV and 15mA, showing conversion to V and A and a check.
safety: Do not alter real wiring or voltage settings to test the calculation.
Only trained, authorized personnel may measure energized parts using the prescribed method.
mfg1-surface-lesson-041.summary:
Align units before substitution.
Check what is held constant and the resistor model’s applicable range.

mfg1-surface-lesson-042.title: Organize current and voltage in series and parallel circuits
mfg1-surface-lesson-042.objective:
Distinguish equivalent-resistance calculations from quantities shared by components.
Check conservation at junctions and around closed loops.

paragraphs.title: Current is shared in series
paragraphs.text:
In a series circuit with resistors along one path, the same current flows through each resistor. Equivalent resistance is R=R1+R2. Voltage drops depend on resistance; two resistors do not necessarily have equal voltages.
Ideal 4Ω and 8Ω resistors in series give 12Ω. At 24V across the circuit, current is 2A and the voltage drops are 8V and 16V.

paragraphs.title: Parallel branches share terminal voltage
paragraphs.text:
In a parallel circuit with branches between the same two nodes, each branch has the same voltage. Current divides according to branch resistance. Equivalent resistance follows 1/R=1/R1+1/R2; for two resistors, R=R1R2/(R1+R2).
Positive finite resistances in parallel give an equivalent resistance smaller than the smaller resistor. Identify the nodes rather than confusing this with series addition.

paragraphs.title: Check junction and loop balances
paragraphs.text:
Kirchhoff’s current law states that the sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving it. The voltage law states that the signed sum of voltage changes around a closed loop is zero. With one source and resistors, source voltage corresponds to the sum of voltage drops.
Choose current directions and a loop direction first, and use consistent signs for the source and drops. If values do not balance, also check how the diagram was read and the measurement conditions.

paragraphs.title: Compare two connections
paragraphs.text: Ideal 6Ω and 3Ω resistors in parallel give 6×3/(6+3)=2Ω. At 6V, branch currents are 1A and 2A, totaling 3A. Connecting the same resistors in series gives 9Ω and is a different circuit. These are paper examples, not instructions to modify wiring.

terms.meaning: A connection placing resistors or other components sequentially on one path.
A connection making branches between the same two nodes.
The value representing several resistors as one overall resistance.
A reduction in voltage across a resistor or other current-carrying component.

mfg1-surface-lesson-042.activity:
Explain individual and total voltages in the 4Ω and 8Ω series example.
Write the junction current balance for the 6Ω and 3Ω parallel example.
safety: Do not change real equipment connections for study.
Power-off alone does not establish safety; follow equipment-specific safety procedures.
mfg1-surface-lesson-042.summary:
Series components share current; parallel branches share terminal voltage.
Check equivalent resistance and current/voltage balances.
